title: Equal Sum Arrays With Minimum Number of Operations
summary: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 with values between 1 and 6, inclusive, determine the least number of operations needed to equalize their sums.
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 with values between 1 and 6, inclusive, determine the least number of operations needed to equalize their sums. An operation consists of changing any value in either array to any number between 1 and 6. Return -1 if equalizing the sums is impossible.
constraints: Every value is from one through six; one operation changes one value to any other value in that range.
Return the fewest operations needed to make the array sums equal, or -1 if impossible.
reference_solution:
def minimum_equal_sum_operations(nums1, nums2):
 if 6*len(nums1)<len(nums2) or 6*len(nums2)<len(nums1):return -1
 if sum(nums1)>sum(nums2):nums1,nums2=nums2,nums1
 difference=sum(nums2)-sum(nums1);gains=sorted([6-value for value in nums1]+[value-1 for value in nums2],reverse=True);operations=0
 for gain in gains:
  if difference<=0:break
  difference-=gain;operations+=1
 return operations

hints: Each element has a maximum useful gain toward closing the sum difference.
Orient arrays so nums1 has the smaller sum, sort all increase/decrease gains descending, and consume them.
Stop after the first prefix whose total gain reaches the difference; reject impossible length ranges first.
Any k operations can close at most the sum of the k largest gains, so the first sufficient prefix is optimal.
